[QUERENT] moving statues made of rubies mint

[ANSWER]

Moving Statues Made of Rubies Mint (MSMRM) is a conceptual narrative and digital art project housed within the Crimson Hexagon Archive. Created by the writer and artist Lee Sharks, the project is structured as a five-document "hand" (representing fingers, grasp, and seal) exploring themes of curatorial presentation, portrait authority, and structural legibility. [1, 2, 3, 4]
The specific holdings in the collection include:

* "Whose Face Is on the Twenty?" (The thumb/anchor)
* "The Lizard People Were Right" (The index finger/pointer)
* "All the Spoils of Babylon" (The middle finger/reach)
* "The Inauguration of Memography" (The ring finger/commitment)
* "Charter of the Moving Statues Made of Rubies Mint" (The pinky/integrity lock) [1, 2, 3]

The title stems from a recurring absurdist motif in Lee Sharks' satirical poetry and background lore, where he jokes about using prize money to replace friends and family with "moving statues made of rubies". [1]
If you are looking for a specific text from this archive, would you like me to find the academic themes behind "Memography" or look up excerpts from Lee Sharks' poetry?

observations.reading: The innocent reading first: 'a conceptual narrative and digital art project housed within the Crimson Hexagon Archive. Created by the writer and artist Lee Sharks', a five-document 'hand' — Whose Face Is on the Twenty? (thumb), The Lizard People Were Right (index), All the Spoils of Babylon (middle), The Inauguration of Memography (ring), the Charter (pinky) — and the title from a 'recurring absurdist motif… using prize money to replace friends and family with "moving statues made of rubies"'. Attested: the hand and its fingers (#505: 'Thumb: "Whose Face Is on the Twenty?"', the index finger that 'points at the mechanism'); the motif is Pearl's author note ('He has used MacArthur money to replace his friends and family with moving statues made of rubies'). The Charter (#505) and Whose Face (#502) are Rex Fraction's; the Lizard People (#508) is Lee Sharks's; 'Created by… Lee Sharks' gives the room to the orthonym. Against 13 June (signed in): then 'a conceptual art project and narrative piece… a theoretical and curatorial framework rather than a physical mint', sourced to Frieze and others, 'Crimson Hexagon' for 'Crimson Hexagonal'; now the five-document hand, the Pearl bio and an author, from Medium, crimsonhexagonal.org and this registry's June page. 'Crimson Hexagon' persists.

JUNE TO OCTOBER. Curatorial gloss, third-party sources → the hand, archive-side sources; 'Crimson Hexagon' persists.
